questions.stem: A Mac user downloads software and sees three file types: .dmg, .pkg, and .app. Which pairing of each to its role is correct?

choices.text: .dmg is a virtual CD; .pkg runs a setup wizard; .app is a self-contained application bundle
.dmg is the application itself; .pkg is a virtual CD; .app is a setup wizard
.dmg is a setup wizard; .pkg is the application bundle; .app is a disk image
All three are identical formats with different extensions

questions.explanation: .dmg = disk image (virtual CD). .pkg = installer package (setup wizard). .app = self-contained application bundle.
questions.trap: It is easy to mix .dmg and .app, but the .app is the actual program; the .dmg is just the container you mount.

questions.stem: What is the standard way to uninstall a .app on macOS?

choices.text: Run an .exe uninstaller from the Applications folder
Drag the .app from Applications to the Trash
Use Disk Utility to erase the volume

questions.explanation: macOS apps are self-contained bundles, so uninstalling is typically as simple as dragging the .app from Applications to the Trash.
questions.trap: macOS does not run .exe files; that's a Windows concept.

questions.stem: Time Machine is set up on a Mac. Which backup schedule does it follow by default?

choices.text: Only when the user manually starts it

questions.explanation: Time Machine performs hourly, daily, and weekly backups automatically.
questions.trap: Manual-only is wrong; Time Machine's value is its hands-off cadence.

questions.stem: Which macOS feature is the direct equivalent of Windows BitLocker (full-disk encryption)?
questions.explanation: FileVault is the macOS full-disk encryption feature, equivalent in role to Windows BitLocker.
questions.trap: Keychain stores passwords and certificates; it is not full-disk encryption.

questions.stem: Which macOS feature launches a systemwide search with Cmd + Space?
questions.explanation: Spotlight is the systemwide search tool launched with Cmd + Space. It finds files, apps, and even suggests websites.
questions.trap: Mission Control spreads open windows; it is not the search tool.

questions.stem: An app freezes on macOS. Which key combination opens the Force Quit menu to shut it down?
questions.explanation: Cmd + Option + Esc opens the Force Quit menu on macOS to terminate a frozen app.
questions.trap: Ctrl + Alt + Del is Windows; macOS uses Cmd + Option + Esc.

questions.stem: What does Mission Control on macOS do, and how is it commonly accessed on a trackpad?

choices.text: It is the Apple ID password vault, accessed via the Keychain icon
It is the encrypted backup service, accessed by clicking the Time Machine icon
It is the systemwide search bar opened with Cmd + Space
It spreads all open windows for an overview and lets you create multiple desktops (Spaces); accessed by swiping up with three fingers

questions.explanation: Mission Control spreads out all open windows and lets you create multiple desktops (Spaces). Three-finger swipe up on the trackpad opens it.
questions.trap: Cmd + Space is Spotlight (search), not Mission Control.

questions.stem: Keychain on macOS is described as a digital safe-deposit box. Which three items does it securely store, all encrypted with the login password?

choices.text: Operating system files, kernel modules, and drivers

questions.explanation: Keychain securely stores passwords, certificates, and private notes, encrypted by the user's login password.
questions.trap: Media (photos/videos) is iCloud Photos; OS files belong to macOS itself.

questions.stem: Which macOS feature allows starting work on a Mac and seamlessly continuing it on an iPhone or iPad?
questions.explanation: Continuity lets you start work on a Mac and pick it up on your iPhone or iPad.
questions.trap: Spotlight is the systemwide search; it doesn't move work between devices.

questions.stem: After Software Update applies a Rapid Security Response (RSR), how is the installed RSR identified next to the OS version number?

choices.text: By a Greek letter, like alpha or beta
By a single letter appended to the version number
It is hidden and never visible to the user
By a four-digit year added to the build number

questions.explanation: An installed RSR is shown as a letter appended next to the OS version number.
questions.trap: RSRs are visible; Apple specifically marks them so admins can confirm they are present.
